state.initial_idea: Slaag Group: platform for Afrikaans-speaking families in South Africa. First business (year 1, 100% Afrikaans): academic support helping parents of Grade 4-7 children prepare for tests/exams. Pain: last-minute, stressful, conflict-laden manual quizzing from textbooks; parent guilt; kids who don't pass or underachieve; kids lying about preparation. Future (not now): schools group subscriptions, teachers (flipped classroom, pre/post quizzes), private tutors, English-speaking users, other education/non-education extensions for Afrikaner households.

rounds.a: AI-drafted content trees/questions/model answers from Slaag-owned textbook copies, reviewed+approved by Afrikaans teachers before learners see them; small launch textbook set.

rounds.q: Launch engine scope: diagnostic + KT mastery + remediation + spaced review only?
rounds.a: Bigger: everything. All 7 techniques (diagnostic, adaptive learning/difficulty, knowledge tracing, mastery-based progression, adaptive retrieval, spaced repetition, error-based remediation, interleaving) plus per-child tuning from marks must be in first release.
No WhatsApp. Parents get email notifications. Parents and kids get push notifications via hybrid mobile apps published to app stores: Capacitor-wrapped TanStack Start web application.

rounds.q: Must content be textbook-specific, or CAPS-topic bank + per-textbook page maps?
rounds.a: Hybrid: shared CAPS-topic question bank per grade/subject as base; per-textbook page/chapter maps to topics; per-textbook overrides of definitions/model answers where wording differs.

Accepted: diagnostic <=15 min per test scope; prep session 10-20 min; LLM grader >=90% agreement with teacher 'good enough' on reviewed sample; plan covers every in-scope concept >=1x and every weak concept >=2x before test date; track (not gate) that plan-completers rate tests ok/good more often.

In-app only credits (no monetary value/no shop) earned for activities (add test, complete session, early finish, streaks); unlock levels, badges, cosmetic items (avatar/mascot outfits). Parents may optionally set a real-life reward at a credit target, tracked by Slaag but fulfilled by parent.

Gr 4-7 content-heavy subjects: NS&Tech (NS in Gr7), Sosiale Wetenskappe (Geskiedenis + Aardrykskunde), EBW Gr7; 2-3 most-used Afrikaans textbooks each; all 4 terms; every question teacher-approved. Wiskunde, languages, LV/LO post-launch.

rounds.q: Is persistent per-child concept mastery the core, with tests/exams as lenses?
rounds.a: No - each test/exam stands alone: own plan, mastery starts fresh per assessment. (Within an assessment, ad-hoc sessions still feed the plan; per-child tuning from marks is algorithm-level, not carried mastery.)

Accepted: 'Who's studying?' switcher in parent's signed-in app with 4-digit child PIN, parent areas need re-auth/biometric; child's own device: one-time sign-in (username/password or social), stays signed in; multiple children on one device switch via PIN; parent can reset PIN/password. No email links.

Accepted: push+email <=5 min on child test/exam add/edit; session-time push to child+parent, missed after 2h no-start -> logged + parent alert; push+email <=5 min on session completion with score, weak topics, next step; weekly Sunday-evening digest email; per-child parent dashboard (upcoming tests/exams, readiness % per test, weak topics, credits/reward goal, full session log incl. ad-hoc); parent can mute any alert type per channel.

Priced per family (flat), max 3 children per family. Card payment via PayFast with onsite checkout; Slaag can initiate card update flow onto PayFast. (Web-only checkout in store apps and 7-day grace not explicitly addressed - carry as assumptions.)

rounds.q: Scheduling rules (study windows, slot limits, overrides, auto-reschedule)?
rounds.a: Simpler: no study windows. Slaag suggests one next session date/time at a time; child or parent accepts or changes it.

Accepted: Afrikaans UI at Gr4 reading level; no shaming language, encouraging line + model answer immediately; celebration animation + praise + credits at session end; parent-visible credit table; smooth on 2GB RAM Android; <5MB data per 15-min session; POPIA with parental consent recorded at registration.

user_detail_notes: Parent: register via Google/Microsoft/Apple only (no local password); agrees to monthly subscription; first charge pro-rata, billing runs on 2nd of month.

Parent with active subscription creates child accounts it owns/controls. Child: only 'name' required; Grade + Province; per-subject textbook confirmation; subjects activated selectively (can add later).
Child login: Google/Microsoft/Apple OR username/password. Open question: social-login UX for kids; kids often use sibling/parent phones (shared devices).

Year-1 surface: responsive web app (laptop + mobile browser); all registration/payment on web. Later: Android app (priority) for push notifications to parent and child; ~10% parents on Apple; many Gr6-7 kids own Android devices.
Tests (small, within term) vs Exams (end of term, consolidated). Parent or child adds test/exam: date + scope via textbook content-tree selection or page ranges (e.g. 56-67, 88-95).

Slaag evaluates content volume vs time until test/exam, then suggests and negotiates date/time of 'prep sessions'. Prep session = secret sauce, multiple forms, grows sophisticated over time. User will expand on prep session + other features next.
Parent alerted when child adds test/exam; can view and revise details incl. prep session date/time.
Kids+parents alerted when prep session time arrives; kids can manually trigger a prep session.

Prep session forms: Diagnostic Assessment (adaptive, minimal time; finds gaps/misconceptions); Adaptive Learning paradigm with Knowledge Tracing (per-concept mastery) and Mastery-Based progression; Adaptive Retrieval Practice; Spaced Repetition; Error-Based Remediation; Interleaving. Distinguish Adaptive Learning (paradigm) / Knowledge Tracing (learner model) / Spaced Retrieval (reinforcement).
Question types: MCQ + written definition/paragraph assessed against model answer by inexpensive LLM classifier (user mentioned 'JEV'); model answer shown immediately.

After session: result shown + parent alerted; child praised; system suggests next step. Child can create ad-hoc sessions on part of scope; later generated sessions account for them. All sessions planned/missed/completed logged and communicated to parent.
After test date: child rates tough/ok/good, optionally captures % or marks -> performance record + feedback loop to tune algorithm per child.
Experience: non-stressful, fun animations, light language, humour. Gamification: credits for activities (loading tests, completing sessions).
